newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Canada calls the tune.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Canada calls the tune.

text.p: The Australian bond market scrambled back from an initial hefty sell-off, but failed to pull back on its spread differentials against Canada, which outperformed the dollar bloc.

Switching to Canadian assets from Australia after Standard & Poor's raised Canada's outlook on its foreign currency debt to stable from negative was sighted as one of a combination of factors that prompted local long yields to spike some 10 basis points at the start of trading.
The Australian/Canadian 10-year yield spread ballooned to some 135 basis points just after the opening, its highest level since April last year.
The 10-year margin to the U.S. also leapt to over 120 basis points, but this proved to be the peak and having widened from 100 basis points in the space of a week.
The U.S. market itself was fairly subdued ahead of Wednesday's first leg of the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The second installment of his testimony has been reset for March 5 instead of Thursday.

However, while Australian debt managed to pare their early loses, New Zealand bonds closed weaker after today's quarterly employment survey confirmed that the economy continues to grow. N.Z. average hourly ordinary time earnings rose 0.7 percent in the November quarter to 3.5 percent on the year.

Australian wages data will also be the key focus for the local market over the next couple of days with the latest report on enterprise bargaining agreements due on Wednesday and final average weekly earnings on Thursday.
